title: Ran taskkill /IM python.exe /T on a shared PC, killing unrelated production processes
details:
**What happened:** A background `python dashboard_server.py --help` call hung (no --help handling in that script). Model ran `taskkill //F //IM python.exe //T` to clean it up, which killed every python.exe process on the machine, including an unrelated production `live_poll.py` data-collection daemon and an operational dashboard server on port 8765 that were already running before this session touched anything.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment yet; caught and self-reported by the model before the user noticed.
**Repro:** On a machine with other long-running python processes, back a hung/backgrounded python command into a corner and reach for `taskkill /IM python.exe /T` instead of killing the specific PID.
**Evidence:** repo ~/Dev-Mw/AROS_Reverse_Eng_260803, tools/dashboard_server.py (no CLI arg parsing, `--help` just hangs waiting on server loop), restarted PIDs 11004 (live_poll.py) and 32616 (dashboard_server.py) after the incident.
**Cause:** Model chose a name-based, blast-radius-unbounded kill command to solve a local problem (one hung backgrounded call) instead of targeting the specific PID, on a machine explicitly documented in this project's CLAUDE.md as running unrelated always-on production processes.
